title: BENEFITS provider tool: Spain

wellby_spine.label: €14,050 (HM Treasury's £13,000 per WELLBY at 2019 prices, uprated to £16,300 at 2024 prices, then PPP-adjusted)
wellby_spine.provenance_note: The HM Treasury GBP 13,000 (2019) spine, uprated and PPP-adjusted to Spain (0.861941). Transfer with a stated adjustment; an explicit modelling assumption flagged transfer-from-UK. The `value` field is documentation, not an input: no formula in the tool reads it. The WELLBY bands in `data.outcomes` were multiplied through at build time, so editing this number changes nothing on the page until those bands are rebuilt. check_drift.py asserts that the label still quotes it, so an edit here cannot silently leave the two disagreeing.

capacity_caveat: The capacity and shock model is INDICATIVE: demand elasticities and staff ratios are mostly UK register values, and the share of households losing an earner is the UK model's own share applied to Spain's working-age households. It is not calibrated to Spain.
provenance: Income effect from EUROMOD v3.8.6 run on EU-SILC data (2024 wave, income reference year 2023, policy system ES_2023), as in the D2.2 Spain tool. Provider values are per person served, in EUR at 2024 prices. Every value carries its source and a grade in its own note; a value borrowed from another country is marked.

provenance_note.elastCentral: UK register value for Jobcentre Plus work coaches (demand moves one-for-one with unemployment, range 0.8 to 1.2), transferred unadjusted

provenance_note.unitCost: EUR 1,080, converted from the UK tool's unit cost for Jobcentre Plus work coaching, GBP 1,200 per participant, itself an assumption declared at the 2024 base. services.flag: Unit: one participant in an employment-support episode. Outcome value: borrowed from another country without adjustment. +0.46 WELLBY for a move from unemployment into work (Clark et al. 2018, the Britain fixed-effects coefficient HM Treasury's guidance uses), valued at the WELLBY value for Spain, then staged as in the UK tool: effect 0.11 / 0.30 / 0.46 x attribution 0.20 / 0.22 / 0.27. services.flag: Unit: one claim supported. Outcome value: borrowed from another country with a stated adjustment. Income effect: the extra-income figure. Health-service use avoided: Liverpool Citizens Advice on Prescription (SSM Population Health 2025), an instrumental-variable study on linked NHS records: GBP 91 per person a year (95% CI 44 to 107) at 2023 prices, an impact, so attribution 1.0. The saving is per household member; the central counts the client only, the high counts every member (20,773 members of 8,205 client households). Uprated to 2024-25 on ONS L8GG and converted at household-consumption PPP (OECD, 2024, the factor of 0.861941 per GBP the Spain tool uses for every transfer from the UK). The advice covered benefits, debt and housing together. services.flag: Unit: one recipient for a year. Outcome value: an assumption. Excluded for every country: no robust per-person effect exists. Randomised evidence shows small effects on food insecurity (for example Briefel et al., -2.8 points) and none on wellbeing; the Greek DIATROFI school-meal trial is a different service. The tool shows the income effect only, as a floor.

A year of out-of-home care costs EUR 48,937 per child (Consejeria de Bienestar Social, Junta de Comunidades de Castilla-La Mancha (2026), Orden 47/2026, de 8 de abril, por la que se actualizan las cantidades de la Orden 146/2024 (concierto social acogimiento residencial de menores 2024-2028), DOCM 16.04.2026 (full text reproduced by INAP 'La Administracion al Dia'), EUR 138 x 365 days at 2026 prices, uprated on the GDP deflator.). provenance_note.aff3: The UK's modelled share of working-age units whose employment income falls at 3pp (2.176418 per cent of working-age benefit units), applied to this country's own WORKING-AGE unit count. Chain: 19,316.723 thousand units x 0.7832846446 x 0.02176418 = 329.3 thousand. The middle factor is the working-age share of units this surface reports, n_units_working_age_sample 23,327 over n_units 29,781 (europe/Spain/outputs/dial_grid.json meta, and surface_provenance.json lines 18 to 19). The base is matched rather than the rate restated because this tree carries no all-household unit count for the UK at all: the UK frame is filtered to working age before the engine output is read (uk/model/Code_FRS_23_24/09_build_dial_grid.py line 239), so restating the UK share over all households would need a figure no committed file holds. LIMITATION: the working-age share is the ratio of two UNWEIGHTED sample counts applied to a WEIGHTED unit count, because this surface carries no weighted working-age unit total; it is the closest base the committed data supports, not an exact one. The two working-age definitions match, at least one adult aged 18 to 64 in both (europe/common/adapter.py line 30; uk/model/Code_FRS_23_24/03_build_policyengine_dataset.py line 492). The UK figure counts units, not people: its shock zeroes one earner per selected unit. It is not a count of everyone in an affected unit, which would be about 2.4 times larger. Borrowed from the UK with a stated adjustment, not nationally derived: this country's own surface carries no affected-unit count.

meta.note: ES Analyst response surface. Single-reform magnitude grids; one lever per point; baseline is the zero point of each dial. WEVM and decile contributions in EUR MILLIONS, equivalised, median-anchored, AROP-floored. Native 2023 income reference year (EU-SILC 2024 wave); nominal EUR, no uprating, no PPP (downstream). Real-build logic per country (ES yem/yse; IT +yseev; EL +yemre/ysere); unemployment flips nested for monotonicity.

units.fiscal: EUR millions versus baseline; net_exchequer_cost_m = benefit - tax - sic - sic_employer, positive is a cost to the exchequer
units.poverty: levels, not deltas: headcounts of people in thousands, poverty gaps in EUR millions, anchored_bhc_threshold_cur in EUR of equivalised annual income, with population_k and units_k as the denominators a rate needs
units.winlose: the weighted count of households with a gain, and with a loss, each over the weighted count of all households, times 100. Shares of households, not of people, unlike every poverty headcount in the same object, which counts people. Both rows are labelled with this base on the tool face.

meta.poverty_basis: Two thresholds, both emitted at every point. RELATIVE (relative_*): 60% of that point's own weighted median equivalised (OECD-modified) household disposable income, the published AROP convention and the same line the social weight uses as its floor; it moves with the reform, so a reform that lowers the median lowers the line and can cut the measured count without raising anyone's income. ANCHORED (anchored_*): the same 60%-of-median line computed once at the zero-magnitude baseline point and held fixed across every point of every dial, emitted as anchored_bhc_threshold_cur so it is auditable; internally defined, needing no external source, and the right comparison of a reform against its own baseline. ANCHORED IS NOT ABSOLUTE: the absolute_* fields mean a fixed EXTERNAL base year and stay null because no sourced one exists for ES, IT or EL. The AHC fields are null throughout because the EUROMOD per-unit layer carries no housing-cost concept. All other field names follow the UK surface exactly.
meta.rebuild: Built on EUROMOD v3.8.6, on a COMPLETED input conversion. Every input variable a live 2023 policy reads, for which the EUROMOD input data codebook publishes a recipe and whose sources the public EU-SILC user database carries, is populated from that recipe: Spain carries 68 populated input columns, Greece 55, Italy 44. The consequential ones are Spain's pension and unemployment decompositions and its rent, mortgage and private-pension deductions; Greece's property tax, which is the ENFIA the model reads and passes through; and Italy's contract class, without which no employer contribution fires at all. A surface is a function of its inputs, so reproducing a stored surface is not the test; the test is agreement with each country's own published EUROMOD baseline, recorded in europe/docs/BASELINE_VALIDATION.md. Conventions this surface holds: the stable sort in build_grid.point_from_pu and in wevm._weighted_median / wevm.wevm_by_decile, the two-sided pit_give grid, and the fiscal and poverty objects emitted in the same pass, fiscal by the method of re_emit.py. Poverty carries both a relative (moving) and an anchored (held at baseline) threshold; see poverty_basis.
